label: food_detect_start
note: tool_pose is the CONFIGURED TOOL frame, not the flange: the arm carries a 120 mm z-offset for the 2F-85. The utensil adds more. Measured camera-to-tine-tip is ~105 mm, so the reported point lands within a few cm of the real tip -- good enough to report and to stand off by, NOT good enough for the 4 mm flesh/bowl window, which is terminated on torque instead.
utensil_note: The utensil is fixed to the arm and so is the camera, so at this pose it occupies the SAME pixels in every frame: (646-652, 464)-(756, 718-719) across four runs. Stored here instead of detected: a 'spoon' query once returned the whole BOWL box (the spoon sits in the bowl in the image), which then suppressed every berry as 'inside the utensil'. Re-measure if the utensil is changed or re-gripped. tip = top-centre of the box.
pose_note: Chosen 2026-09-23 with J2 ~+8 deg (arm leaning toward the table) instead of -9.7: same camera orientation (J4 compensates, J2+J4 unchanged), but the camera sits ~120 mm nearer the base, so no berry is hidden behind the utensil and J2 holding torque roughly halves. Then +17 mm X to bring the top of the rim into frame and -20 mm Z for J6 margin: 5.4 deg from its -120.3 limit, was 1.1. Full rim AND a clear view past the utensil is not possible at this bowl size -- the bowl is ~560 px tall, the clear area above the utensil tip ~460 px; this frames the rim top at the image edge.
camera_to_tip_note: FORK, 2026-09-23. Two independent closures agree: ruler tine-tips-to-bare-table 7 in (177.8 mm) against a sensor bare-table depth of 438.8 mm -> 261.0 mm; camera case to tip 10.5 in (266.7 mm) minus the 6.7 mm case-to-depth-frame offset found with the knife -> 260.0 mm. Stored as 265: the knife, closed the same way, proved ~5 mm short in a hover test, and erring long keeps every stop higher. Caution learned here: at food_detect_start the point straight below the tip is the bowl's outer wall (407 mm), not table -- close against bare table, not 'under the tip'.
approach_stop_note: Real-world rule (user, 2026-09-23): stop 10 mm above any surface being approached. 5 mm was seen in practice and judged too close. The PUNCH into food uses floor + food height / 3 instead.
utensil_tip_note: FORK tip pixel set to u=658 (was 707, the top-centre of the fork's image box). At a 10 mm hover the user saw the fork ~10 mm too far left (image-left = the user's left = +Y); at that depth 10 mm is ~49 px of tip pixel, which lands on u=658 -- the column of the knife tip (657-659) and of the fork's handle in the gripper, i.e. the tool axis. The fork head is wide and curled to image-right, so its box centre is NOT where it meets the food.
aim_offset_note: Base-frame (x, y) aim correction applied in OVER, user-confirmed by eye at a 10 mm hover on 2026-09-24 ('this looks perfect'). X +5 mm: the fork's tines extend forward, so aim into the bulk of the flesh. Y -6 mm (away from the user): the detected centre is right, but the fork head curves, so the tines meet the food ~5-7 mm off the tool axis. Fork-specific: re-check when the utensil changes. Image at food_detect_start: +X = up, +Y = left (user's side).
punch_note: NOMINAL margin above the measured bowl floor. 2026-09-24: floor + 7 mm shallow; floor + 2 mm picked a berry up; user then asked for 7 mm deeper than floor + 7 -> 0 nominal. The REAL gap is ~5-10 mm: camera_to_tip is stored long (265 vs 260-261 measured) and the user sees the nominal 10 mm hover as 15-20 mm by eye; the floor is also read in a ring BESIDE the food, where the concave bowl is higher. Do not go below 0 nominal without re-measuring camera_to_tip.
